answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a fixed bond before its votes count, with slashing if peers detect forged identity behavior. Because the bond is per identity, an attacker flooding the network must lock fresh capital for every fake agent, so cost grows linearly with sybils instead of staying flat. Picture capital as a crystal: each identity is one facet cut from a finite treasury, and a pearl of value sits locked under every knoll of claimed reputation, forfeited the moment forgery is proven.
